title: The Girl Who Forgot Her Name

shots.visual_event: Arin enters a carriage lined with thousands of hanging brass name tags; each tag whispers in a different voice.
shots.dialogue_audio: Conductor, over speaker: “Door One collects what passengers stop defending.”

shots.visual_event: A rust-red blur tackles Arin away from a tag reaching for his chest; reveal Saira with silver compass necklace.
shots.dialogue_audio: Saira: “Say your name. Now.” Arin: “Arin Rao.”

shots.visual_event: Arin repeats his name while letters vanish from his blank ticket; Saira presses her compass to her heart.
shots.dialogue_audio: Saira: “Again. Before the carriage eats it.”

shots.visual_event: A tag marked only by editorial typography SAIRA SEN / 1998 swings behind her; Arin realizes her era.
shots.dialogue_audio: Arin: “You’ve been here since 1998?” Saira: “It’s still 1998.”

shots.visual_event: The carriage lights fail in sequence. A child-sized silhouette with cracked luminous hands watches through the forest of tags.
shots.dialogue_audio: Child whisper: “He brought me another name.”

shots.visual_event: Arin and Saira slam the next door shut; the brass tag in Arin’s fist now carries Meera’s fingerprint, not text.

end_card.text: SHE HAS BEEN SIXTEEN FOR 28 YEARS
